To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mouse and human CD1c+ CD11b+ dendritic cells are specialized in promoting IL-17 cytokine responses.

1) mouse lung and gut laminal propria CD11+ DC populations are comprised of two subsets; FLT3-dependent CD24+ CD64- DCs and contaminant CSF-1 receptor-dependent CD24- CD64+ macrophage; 2) loss of CD24 + CD11+ DCs abrogate CD4+ T cells-mediated IL-17 production in steady state as well as after Aspergillis fumigatus (Af) challenge; 3
IRF4-dependent dendritic cells (IRF4 DCs) are specialized in driving IL17 responses in both mice and humans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of dendritic cells (CD11c+) in the lung and gut mucosa and their role in the induction of Th17 cell responses in the steady state and after infection.
the identification of novel immune cells and their role in the regulation of immunity to infection, with particular emphasis on fungal pathogens.
the identification of the mechanisms that underpin the development and function of the CD11b+ dendritic cells in mucosal tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD11b+ CD24+CD4+ DCs are specialized in driving IL 17 responses in both human and mouse.
the IRF4+CD11b + DCs in mouse and human control IL-17 cytokine responses.
the authors have identified a novel DC subset in mice and humans that are specialized in promoting IL-17 production by CD4+ T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IRF4-dependent mouse lung and gut CD24+CD4+CD11b DCs are functionally equivalent to human CD1c+CD4+ DCs, and are specialized in promoting Th17 responses in both species.
the IRF4-dependent DC subsets in both mice and humans are specialized to drive IL-17 responses.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD11b+CD24+CD64+ DC subset in mouse is specialized in driving mucosal IL-17 responses and is the equivalent of human CD1c+CD14+ DC subset.
we have defined the first DC subset in mice that is specialized in driving Th17 cell responses and that we have identified a human equivalent of this DC subset.
